transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Saffron Head of Platform), Elliot Moore (CTO), Samir Patel (SRE)

Summary:
- Intro to Redwood quickstart / free credits and options to move to Dedicated or Private.
- Saffron wants low time-to-first-token for internal devs, clear compliance (KMS, audit logs), and a plan for a pilot that may require VPC or on-prem later.
- Action items: security docs, capacity estimate, sample perf bench.

Topics:
- PLG/self-serve onboarding, free credits, time-to-first-token
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency
- Sizing and expected throughput; bench plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood platform team, and with me is Diego Ramos, our solutions engineer.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Hi Maya, hi Diego. Quick intro — Saffron's building an assistant layer for enterprise document workflows, lots of PII in some customers and a mix of on-prem and cloud customers. I'm Priya, head of platform. Elliot and Samir are on to talk infra and SRE constraints.
[00:35] Elliot Moore: Yeah thanks, we want to understand how fast we can get devs to first token and what the migration path looks like if we need private deployment later. This is mostly evaluation of Redwood hosted first.
[00:50] Diego Ramos: Totally. Today we'll run through quickstart steps for the Hosted API, free credits, typical time-to-first-token for teams, then go into Dedicated and Private options — VPC, on-prem. We'll also cover security controls and what we need to see for a pilot.
[01:10] Samir Patel: One question up front — data residency. Some of our customers require EU-only residency, and a few require data not to be logged at all. How does Redwood handle that?
[01:25] Maya Chen: Good callout. For Hosted we have EU regions and opt-out flags for logging, plus data retention controls. For more stringent needs we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can control log forwarding and use customer-managed KMS. We'll send the SOC2 and the privacy controls doc after the call.
[01:45] Priya Shah: When you say "opt-out flags" — is that per-tenant via the API or a contract-level toggle?
[01:55] Diego Ramos: Right now we support it at the project/account level for Hosted with contractual addendums for retention terms. For Dedicated/Private you get full control to flip it per environment.
[02:15] Elliot Moore: Cost is another axis. If we start with Hosted and scale, is there an easy lift to Dedicated without rewriting code?
[02:30] Maya Chen: Yes — one of our design goals is a consistent API so switching routing from hosted to your Dedicated pool is a config-level change. No SDK rewrites. There are also quantized model variants that reduce cost for some workloads; we'll point you to profiles.
[02:55] Priya Shah: Great. For time-to-first-token — we've seen teams take anywhere from the same day to a couple weeks depending on auth. What's the realistic path for our devs?
[03:10] Diego Ramos: For pure API calls with our SDK, typical is under an hour to call the first token once API keys are generated and SDK installed. If you add SSO and private networking it adds days to weeks. For PLG dev onramp, we can give credits and example templates so devs hit first token in minutes.
[03:35] Samir Patel: Hmm, we need SAML SSO for internal access and RBAC for route restrictions. Do you provide SSO on Hosted?
[03:45] Maya Chen: Hosted supports SSO for enterprise accounts via SAML; for self-serve accounts it's email/API keys. RBAC is available in the Console for enterprise and Dedicated customers.
[04:05] Elliot Moore: On the security front, we also need encryption with customer KMS — we can’t have vendor-managed keys for some customers. Is customer KMS supported?
[04:20] Diego Ramos: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations. Hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS by default, but we can extend for enterprise contracts. We'll attach the KMS doc in the follow-up.
[04:40] Priya Shah: Can you run us through an expected pilot architecture if we start with Hosted but must move to Private mid-pilot?
[04:55] Diego Ramos: Sure. Step 1: fast onramp — create project, generate API keys, import tokenized prompts. Step 2: run sample traffic via the hosted API with prefix caching enabled and measure real latency. Step 3: if residency or KMS requirements show up, spin a Private control plane in your VPC and switch routing with our edge proxy. The app-level calls remain identical. The main work is networking and certs.
[05:30] Priya Shah: Ok, what about performance — specifically KV cache behavior and cold-start latencies? We get nervous about tail latencies on small models.
[05:45] Diego Ramos: Our runtime maintains per-model KV cache and supports continuous batching. For cold starts we have warmup hooks and preloaded caches on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we have proactive warming for canary tiers but tail can vary. We'll propose a bench to show numbers on your workload.
[06:15] Elliot Moore: Can you quantify "proactive warming"? Are there SLA guarantees around 99th pct?
[06:25] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we can include latency SLOs in the contract. Hosted has published performance profiles per model variant with typical 95th/99th numbers — we use those for expectations. For the pilot we'll run a bench and give you measured p50/p95/p99.
[06:45] Samir Patel: Another operational concern is audit logs — we need structured logs of user calls and tokens for compliance.
[06:55] Diego Ramos: Audit logs are available for enterprise and Dedicated; they include request IDs, timestamps, and headers. For Private you can pipeline logs to Splunk/ELK. Hosted can stream to customer's logging destinations via secure forwarding if contracted.
[07:20] Priya Shah: So the immediate ask from us: 1) can you give us a credit pack to let devs iterate? 2) what's the likely size and cost of Dedicated for our 8–15k daily interactive calls? 3) what security docs do you provide?
[07:40] Maya Chen: Yes to credits — we typically give a dev credit package that covers first two-to-four weeks of early exploration. We'll provide a Dedicated sizing ballpark based on your traffic profile, and the security packet includes SOC2, KMS/HSM notes, SSO/SAML guide, and data residency FAQ.
[08:05] Elliot Moore: For the Dedicated sizing — we might be more bursty: 100–200 concurrent interactive sessions peaking during business hours, average token per request around 350.
[08:20] Diego Ramos: That helps. We'll use that to estimate GPU pool size and batching configs. Quick note: effective cost depends heavily on sequence length distribution and cache hit rate. If you can share token histograms we can be more precise.
[08:40] Samir Patel: We'll pull token histograms and sample latency traces.
[08:45] Priya Shah: Does Redwood do model quantization recommendations? We have some internal evals with 4-bit quantized weights but would like platform-level guidance.
[08:55] Diego Ramos: Yes, our Optimize toolkit suggests quantization profile per workload; some models work well at 4-bit with small quality loss, others not. We'll include model recommendations in the follow-up.
[09:15] Speaker 4: (background) I have a question about billing tags and cost-attribution per team.
[09:22] Maya Chen: Good one — we have cost tags and per-token attribution in the Console. For Dedicated it's at pool or project level with exportable usage reports.
[09:35] Elliot Moore: How would a pilot that starts hosted and migrates to Private handle data migration? Do we need data egress and re-ingestion?
[09:48] Diego Ramos: Usually user data isn't moved — you control what you persist. For model KV caches, if using Private you'd rebuild cache from a warmup plan. For persistent datasets we recommend S3 style mirroring into the private environment, which we can script.
[10:10] Priya Shah: Ok. Another question — compliance audits. We have customers requiring ISO and SOC evidence. How recent are your reports?
[10:20] Maya Chen: We maintain SOC2 Type II reports and ISO certs where relevant; we'll share the latest artifacts behind an NDA if required.
[10:32] Samir Patel: Are there any blockers for us to run early integration tests this week?
[10:38] Maya Chen: No blocker. If you accept the dev credits and we provision the project, your engineers can be calling in minutes. If you need SSO and private networking it takes longer.
[10:50] Elliot Moore: We'd prefer a hybrid: let devs self-serve into Hosted for fast iteration, but the pilot should exercise Dedicated-like configs (like KMS-enabled workflows) to validate migration.
[11:05] Diego Ramos: Makes sense — we can create a sandbox that mimics Dedicated constraints and run the bench.
[11:15] Priya Shah: On the bench, can you simulate our token distribution and 95th percentile latency targets? We want to hit <300ms p95 for interactive flows.
[11:25] Diego Ramos: We'll design the bench with your token histograms and target model. Note that sequence length and KV cache hit rate will be the main levers. We'll try to meet p95 <300ms on Dedicated with right sizing; Hosted is dependent on concurrency and region.
[11:50] Maya Chen: Quick finer point — are you expecting to use function-calling or tool integration patterns that produce many smaller calls, or large single-shot responses?
[12:05] Elliot Moore: Mostly a combination — multi-turn chat with occasional retrieval calls for doc fetches. So we will have mix of short calls and longer answers.
[12:18] Diego Ramos: Good — mixed workloads are where batching and caching help the most. We'll show you tradeoffs and recommended batching window sizes.
[12:30] Priya Shah: Any noteworthy limitations on model variants in Dedicated vs Hosted?
[12:38] Diego Ramos: Generally parity on most open models, but very new architectures may be hosted-only initially; Dedicated has curated model catalog and we can onboard models upon request.
[12:55] Samir Patel: Is there an on-prem package for fully air-gapped customers?
[13:02] Maya Chen: Yes, our Private on-prem option supports air-gapped deployments, though that requires deeper integration and longer lead time — usually several weeks to months depending on environment.
[13:18] Elliot Moore: Ok, let's talk pilot success criteria. For us: devs hitting first token within a day, pilot serving 1–2k daily active users with <300ms p95, and proof that KMS and residency controls meet our compliance. If we get those, we can talk Dedicated contract.
[13:36] Maya Chen: That sounds like a good set. We'll make those the acceptance criteria for the pilot.
[13:45] Priya Shah: Anything we should send you to speed up sizing?
[13:50] Diego Ramos: Token histograms, concurrency patterns, any spike profiles, expected model(s) and sample payloads. Also whether you'll need SAML on Hosted for devs.
[14:05] Priya Shah: We'll send those by Thursday.
[14:12] Maya Chen: Logistics: we'll follow up with a short email that includes dev credit instructions, security packet, and a proposed bench schedule. Diego will include a sizing spreadsheet.
[14:25] Samir Patel: One last quick question — what are typical pitfalls teams hit when going from PLG to Dedicated?
[14:33] Diego Ramos: Biggest ones are underestimating sequence length variability and cache warmup needs, and not providing representative traffic during bench. Also missing network egress rules in VPC which delays Private cutover. We can help with checklists.
[14:55] Elliot Moore: Cool. On competitors — we've also talked with OpenAI and Vertex. Curious how Redwood's cost transparency and routing controls compare.
[15:05] Maya Chen: Our differentiator is routing and cost controls plus unified API across environments. We'll show you cost breakouts per-token and per-route in the Console, and give recommendations like using quantized variants or Dedicated pooling for steady traffic.
[15:30] Priya Shah: Ok, that's helpful. Anything else from your side?
[15:35] Maya Chen: Not from me. Diego, any technical follow-ups?
[15:40] Diego Ramos: I'll follow up with the sizing spreadsheet and a bench plan. Expect that in 48 hours.
[15:48] Priya Shah: Great. We'll assemble token histograms and the compliance checklist and get them over.
[15:55] Maya Chen: Awesome. Let's recap next steps — (1) we send SOC2 and security packet, (2) provision dev credits and a hosted sandbox, (3) Diego builds a Dedicated sizing estimate and bench plan, (4) Saffron provides histograms and residency requirements.
[16:10] Elliot Moore: Works for us. Looking forward to the bench numbers.
[16:16] Samir Patel: Thanks all.
[16:18] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the email and docs.
[16:25] (call ends)

Post-call notes: Redwood to attach security artifacts via secure link (NDA if needed). Saffron to prioritize token distributions and sample requests. Performance bench requested week of 2026-03-16.
